question:
A golfer's shoulder moves through horizontal abduction during the backswing of a drive, from position X to position Y.
Identify the plane and axis of motion for this action at the shoulder joint.
markScheme:
Correct answer: C - Transverse plane / Longitudinal axis.
1 mark for the correct option.

question:
A squash player performs a forehand stroke, with the racket arm moving from a preparation position (A) to point of contact (B).
Identify the main agonist, and the plane and axis of movement, at the right shoulder during this movement.
markScheme: Agonist: pectorals/anterior deltoid (1). Plane: transverse plane (1). Axis: longitudinal axis (1). Max 3 marks.

question: A steeplechase athlete clears a water jump barrier. Identify the type of joint, the joint action and the main agonist at the leading ankle as the athlete clears the barrier.
markScheme: Type of joint: hinge (1). Joint action: dorsiflexion (1). Main agonist: tibialis anterior (1). Max 3 marks.

question:
A sprinter drives the knee upward out of the starting blocks, causing hip flexion.
State the plane and axis around which hip flexion takes place.
markScheme: Plane: sagittal (1). Axis: transverse (1). Max 2 marks.

question:
A weightlifter performs an incline dumbbell press, moving from position A (arms bent, weights at chest level) to position B (arms extended above the chest).
Identify the joint action and main agonist occurring at the shoulder during this movement.
markScheme: Joint action: horizontal flexion/adduction (1). Main agonist: pectoralis major/anterior deltoid (1). Max 2 marks.

question: A weightlifter performs an incline dumbbell press, moving from position A (arms bent, weights at chest level) to position B (arms extended above the chest). Identify the joint action and main agonist occurring at the elbow during this movement.
markScheme: Joint action: extension (1). Main agonist: triceps (1). Max 2 marks.

question:
A volleyball player performs a serve, swinging the hitting arm upward and forward to contact the ball.
(a) State the names of the bones forming the shoulder joint.
(b) State the name of the type of joint found at the shoulder.
(c) Identify the joint action taking place at the shoulder during the upward arm swing, and the main agonist causing this movement.
markScheme:
(a) Humerus and scapula. 1 mark.
(b) Ball and socket. 1 mark.
(c) Action: flexion (1). Agonist: (anterior) deltoid (1). 2 marks.
Max 4 marks.

question:
A performer completes a lateral raise (movement A) followed by a reverse fly (movement B) in a weight-training session.
(a) Identify the correct term for each of the movements A and B.
(b) State the plane and axis involved in these movements.
markScheme:
(a) A = abduction (1); B = adduction (1). 2 marks.
(b) Frontal plane (1); sagittal axis (1). 2 marks.
Max 4 marks.

question:
A javelin thrower's throwing arm moves through two distinct actions at the shoulder during the release phase of the throw.
(a) Identify the two actions occurring at the shoulder during this sequence.
(b) State the name of the agonist muscle for each action.
markScheme:
(a) Rotation (1); extension (1). 2 marks.
(b) Rotation - rotator cuff (1); extension - latissimus dorsi (1). 2 marks.
Max 4 marks.

question: Muscles often work in antagonistic pairs. Explain the term antagonistic pair, using the elbow joint during a bicep curl exercise as an example.
markScheme:
Sub max 2: the elbow joint can flex and extend; during flexion (the curl phase), the biceps brachii acts as the agonist/prime mover; the muscle shortens under tension, reducing the joint angle.
Sub max 2: the triceps brachii acts as the antagonist; it relaxes and lengthens; coordination of the two muscles allows smooth movement around the joint.
Max 4 marks.

question: Using examples from swimming, analyse the movements possible at the shoulder joint.
markScheme:
AO1 (up to 2) - the shoulder is a ball and socket joint, formed from the humerus (head, the 'ball') and scapula (glenoid fossa, the 'socket'); it is triaxial, allowing movement in all three planes.
AO2 (up to 3) - sagittal plane/transverse axis - flexion/extension; frontal plane/sagittal axis - abduction/adduction; transverse plane/longitudinal axis - horizontal flexion (adduction)/horizontal extension (abduction), and rotation.
AO3 (up to 3), with reference to swimming - flexion (eg front crawl arm entry) - anterior deltoid; extension (eg front crawl pull-through) - latissimus dorsi/posterior deltoid; abduction (eg butterfly recovery) - deltoid; adduction - latissimus dorsi/pectorals; rotation (eg freestyle arm rotation) - rotator cuff muscles.
Max 8 marks.

question: Explain why the triceps muscle performs two different types of muscle contraction during the performance of a dip on parallel bars.
markScheme:
Sub max 2: during the upward (pushing) phase of the dip, the triceps performs a concentric contraction; the muscle shortens under tension, causing extension of the elbow.
Sub max 2: during the downward (lowering) phase, the triceps performs an eccentric contraction; the muscle lengthens under tension, controlling/braking the flexion of the elbow against gravity.
Max 4 marks.

question: There are different types of muscle contraction. Compare isotonic and isometric muscle contractions, and concentric and eccentric muscle contractions.
markScheme: Isotonic - contraction resulting in movement (1). Isometric - contraction with no movement/change in muscle length (1). Concentric - shortening of the muscle under tension (1). Eccentric - lengthening of the muscle under tension (1). Max 4 marks.

question:
During the follow-through of a football set-piece kick, flexion occurs at the hip.
Identify which plane and about which axis hip flexion occurs.
markScheme:
Correct answer: C - Sagittal plane and transverse axis.
1 mark for the correct option.
options: A - Transverse plane and longitudinal axis
B - Frontal plane and sagittal axis
C - Sagittal plane and transverse axis
D - Sagittal plane and longitudinal axis
correctOption: C - Sagittal plane and transverse axis

question: During the recovery phase of butterfly stroke, a swimmer's arms move outward to the sides of the body. Identify the type of joint, the main agonist and the joint action at the swimmer's shoulder during this phase.
markScheme: Type of joint: ball and socket (1). Main agonist: deltoid (1). Joint action: abduction (1). Accept first answers only. Max 3 marks.

question: A gymnast performs a controlled dip on parallel bars, lowering from position A to position B. Identify the joint action, the main agonist and the type of isotonic contraction at the elbow from position A to position B.
markScheme: Joint action: flexion (1). Main agonist: triceps brachii (1). Type of isotonic contraction: eccentric (1). Accept first answer only. Max 3 marks.

question: A volleyball player jumps to spike the ball, moving from position A (crouched) to position B (in the air). Identify the main agonist, the type of isotonic muscle contraction and the joint action at the hip during this movement.
markScheme: Main agonist: gluteus maximus/gluteals/hamstrings (1). Type of muscle contraction: concentric (1). Joint action: extension/hyper-extension (1). Accept first answer only. Max 3 marks.

question: During the toe-off phase of a 100 m sprint, the sprinter drives off the right foot. Identify the main agonist, the joint action and the type of contraction at the right ankle during this phase.
markScheme: Main agonist: gastrocnemius (1). Joint action: plantar flexion (1). Type of contraction: concentric/isotonic (1). First answer only. Not calf or soleus for agonist; not dorsiflexion. Max 3 marks.

question: A performer completes a lunge exercise as part of a weight-training programme, moving from Position A (standing) to Position B (lowered). Identify the main agonist, the type of muscle contraction and the joint action at the hip joint during this isotonic movement.
markScheme: Main agonist: gluteals/hamstrings (1). Type of muscle contraction: eccentric (1). Joint action: flexion (1). Accept named individual muscles (biceps femoris/semitendinosus/semimembranosus/gluteus maximus). Max 3 marks.

question: A player performs a chest pass during a game of basketball. Identify the main agonist, the type of muscle contraction and the joint action at the elbow joint during the pass.
markScheme: Main agonist: triceps (brachii) (1). Type of muscle contraction: concentric/isotonic (1). Joint action: extension (1). Accept first answer only; biceps is incorrect. Max 3 marks.

question: A place-kicker takes a conversion attempt in American football. (i) What are the names of the articulating bones of the knee joint of the kicking leg? (ii) What joint action takes place at the knee of the kicking leg as it straightens to strike the ball? (iii) What is the name of the main agonist that causes this action?
markScheme:
(i) Tibia and femur (do not accept fibula/patella). 2 marks.
(ii) Extension. 1 mark.
(iii) Quadriceps/rectus femoris (do not accept 'quads'). 1 mark.
Max 4 marks.

question: A performer drives upward on a leg press machine, from Position A (legs bent) to Position B (legs extended). Identify the joint action, main agonist and type of muscle contraction occurring at the hip and ankle joints during this movement.
markScheme:
Hip: joint action extension (1); main agonist gluteals/hamstrings (1); type of muscle contraction concentric/isotonic (1).
Ankle: joint action plantar flexion (1); main agonist gastrocnemius (1); type of muscle contraction concentric/isotonic (1).
First answers only; accept gluteus maximus/biceps femoris/semi-membranosus/semi-tendinosus; do not accept calf or soleus for the ankle agonist. Max 5 marks.

question: A netball player drives forward. The player's leading leg is extending at the knee as the foot plants. For the movement occurring at the knee joint of the leading leg, name: (i) the axis about which the movement is taking place; (ii) the main agonist causing the movement; (iii) the joint action taking place.
markScheme: (i) Transverse/horizontal axis (1). (ii) Quadriceps/rectus femoris (1). (iii) Extension (1). Max 3 marks.

question: A break-dancer pushes up from a headstand into a handstand freeze, from position A to position B. Name the main agonist at the elbow joint during this movement.
markScheme: Agonist: triceps (brachii). 1 mark.

question: A break-dancer pushes up from a headstand into a handstand freeze, from position A to position B. Name the type of muscle contraction taking place while stationary at position A, and through the movement phase to position B.
markScheme: Position A - stationary - isometric (1). Position B - movement - isotonic/concentric (1). Max 2 marks.

question: In order to perform to their potential, triple jumpers must use their muscles and bones efficiently. A triple jumper drives off the take-off leg during the take-off phase of the hop. Identify: (i) the joint actions involved at the hip and ankle of the take-off leg as the performer leaves the ground; (ii) the names of the main agonists working at the knee and ankle. (iii) Name the lever system operating at the ankle of the take-off foot, and describe its layout. (Diagram description: since this website cannot render a hand-drawn sketch, describe the correct layout of the lever system instead.)
markScheme:
(i) Hip: (hyper)extension. Ankle: plantar flexion. 2 marks.
(ii) Knee agonist: quadriceps. Ankle agonist: gastrocnemius. 2 marks.
(iii) 2nd class lever; resistance/load in the middle, between the fulcrum (ball of the foot) and the effort (calf muscle/Achilles tendon); fulcrum, resistance and effort correctly labelled on a sketch. 3 marks.
Max 7 marks.
